title: A star whose spectrum peaks at 290 nm
caption: Wien's law, λ_maxT = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m K, gives T = 2.898 × 10⁻³/(2.9 × 10⁻⁷) = 9993 K ≈ 10 000 K. The Planck curve for 10 000 K does peak at 290 nm, in the ultraviolet; the visible band (400–700 nm) lies on the long-wavelength side, so the star looks blue-white.
alt: Planck curve for 10000 K against wavelength: it rises to a peak near 290 nm in the ultraviolet and falls slowly through the visible band.
description: The horizontal axis is wavelength in nm; the vertical axis is the relative spectral intensity, scaled so the peak is 1.
The Planck curve for T = 10 000 K peaks at 290 nm, as Wien's law predicts for 2.9 × 10⁻⁷ m.
The shaded band 400–700 nm is visible light: the star's output is already falling there, and most of it is in the ultraviolet.
